title: Kefa and Park
statementMd:
Kefa decided to celebrate his first big salary by going to the restaurant.

He lives by an unusual park. The park is a rooted tree consisting of $*n*$ vertices with the root at vertex $1$. Vertex $1$ also contains Kefa's house. Unfortunaely for our hero, the park also contains cats. Kefa has already found out what are the vertices with cats in them.

The leaf vertices of the park contain restaurants. Kefa wants to choose a restaurant where he will go, but unfortunately he is very afraid of cats, so there is no way he will go to the restaurant if the path from the restaurant to his house contains more than $*m*$ **consecutive** vertices with cats.

Your task is to help Kefa count the number of restaurants where he can go.

## Input

The first line contains two integers, $*n*$ and $*m*$ ($2 ≤ *n* ≤ 10^{5}$, $1 ≤ *m* ≤ *n*$) — the number of vertices of the tree and the maximum number of consecutive vertices with cats that is still ok for Kefa.

The second line contains $*n*$ integers $*a*_{1}, *a*_{2}, ..., *a*_{*n*}$, where each $*a*_{*i*}$ either equals to $0$ (then vertex $*i*$ has no cat), or equals to $1$ (then vertex $*i*$ has a cat).

Next $*n* - 1$ lines contains the edges of the tree in the format "$*x*_{*i*}$ $*y*_{*i*}$" (without the quotes) ($1 ≤ *x*_{*i*}, *y*_{*i*} ≤ *n*$, $*x*_{*i*} ≠ *y*_{*i*}$), where $*x*_{*i*}$ and $*y*_{*i*}$ are the vertices of the tree, connected by an edge.

It is guaranteed that the given set of edges specifies a tree.

## Output

A single integer — the number of distinct leaves of a tree the path to which from Kefa's home contains at most $*m*$ consecutive vertices with cats.

## Note

Let us remind you that a *tree* is a connected graph on $*n*$ vertices and $*n* - 1$ edge. A *rooted* tree is a tree with a special vertex called *root*. In a rooted tree among any two vertices connected by an edge, one vertex is a parent (the one closer to the root), and the other one is a child. A vertex is called a *leaf*, if it has no children.

Note to the first sample test: ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/d5a8860bc0e7f2b3af6eb8d282651cf293b2ca73.png) The vertices containing cats are marked red. The restaurants are at vertices 2, 3, 4. Kefa can't go only to the restaurant located at vertex $2$.

Note to the second sample test: ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/4e80ab2e30751bfa146f6b2be04649530164fd0a.png) The restaurants are located at vertices 4, 5, 6, 7. Kefa can't go to restaurants 6, 7.
statementZhMd:
Kefa 决定去餐厅庆祝自己的第一笔丰厚薪水。

他住在一个不同寻常的公园旁。这个公园是一棵以顶点 $1$ 为根的有根树，共有 $*n*$ 个顶点。顶点 $1$ 还包含 Kefa 的房子。不幸的是，对于我们的主人公来说，公园里还有猫。Kefa 已经知道哪些顶点上有猫。

公园的叶子顶点处有餐厅。Kefa 想选择一家餐厅前往，但不幸的是他非常害怕猫，因此如果从餐厅到他家中的路径上包含超过 $*m*$ 个**连续**的有猫顶点，他就绝不会前往这家餐厅。

你的任务是帮助 Kefa 计算他可以前往的餐厅数量。

## 输入格式

第一行包含两个整数 $*n*$ 和 $*m*$（$2 ≤ *n* ≤ 10^{5}$，$1 ≤ *m* ≤ *n*$）——树的顶点数，以及 Kefa 所能接受的路径上连续有猫顶点的最大数量。

第二行包含 $*n*$ 个整数 $*a*_{1}, *a*_{2}, ..., *a*_{*n}$，其中每个 $*a*_{*i*}$ 要么等于 $0$（表示顶点 $*i*$ 上没有猫），要么等于 $1$（表示顶点 $*i*$ 上有猫）。

接下来的 $*n* - 1$ 行按照格式 "$*x*_{*i*}$ $*y*_{*i*}$"（不含引号）包含树的边（$1 ≤ *x*_{*i*}, *y*_{*i*} ≤ *n*$，$*x*_{*i*}$ ≠ $*y*_{*i*}$），其中 $*x*_{*i*}$ 和 $*y*_{*i*}$ 是由一条边相连的树的顶点。

保证给出的边构成一棵树。

## 输出格式

输出一个整数——树中满足从 Kefa 的家到该叶子顶点的路径上最多包含 $*m*$ 个连续有猫顶点的不同叶子数量。

## 说明

提醒一下，*树*是一个包含 $*n*$ 个顶点和 $*n* - 1$ 条边的连通图。*有根树*是带有一个称为*根*的特殊顶点的树。在有根树中，对于由一条边相连的任意两个顶点，一个顶点是父节点（距离根更近的那个），另一个顶点是子节点。如果一个顶点没有子节点，则称其为*叶子*。

第一个样例的说明：![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/d5a8860bc0e7f2b3af6eb8d282651cf293b2ca73.png) 含有猫的顶点标记为红色。餐厅位于顶点 2、3、4。Kefa 只有位于顶点 $2$ 的餐厅无法前往。

第二个样例的说明：![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/4e80ab2e30751bfa146f6b2be04649530164fd0a.png) 餐厅位于顶点 4、5、6、7。Kefa 无法前往位于顶点 6、7 的餐厅。
